messages.author: ad1a6abcb84542f8
messages.subject: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
parts:
I'm adding some automatic report functionalities into my shiny app.

If I generate the pdf file from the "report.Rnw" via RStudio, it generates ok, but when I generate it via Shiny, the \ref{} stay in "??" instead of changing to the correct number of label it should (for example my PDF report says "figure ??" instead of "figure 2"). Just as if I had not run latex twice when compiling.

Somewhere inside my server.R file I have:

output$downloadPDF <-
    downloadHandler(filename = "report.pdf",
                    content = function(file){
                      # generate PDF
                      library(knitr)
                      knit2pdf("report.Rnw")
                      
                      # copy pdf to 'file'
                      file.copy("report.pdf", file)
                      
                      # delete generated files
                      file.remove("report.pdf", "report.tex",
                                  "report.aux", "report.log","report.out")
                      
                      # delete folder with plots
                      unlink("figure", recursive = TRUE)
                    },
                    contentType = "application/pdf"
    )

Somewhere inside my "report.Rnw" file I have is:

<<MyPlotLabel, fig.lp="fig:", echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Some text here}">>=
plot(gear~carb,data = mtcars, pch = 19, col = 'gray')
@
Figure \ref{fig:MyPlotLabel} shows how it is not possible to do references in Shiny.

Does anyone know what I may be doing wrong?

thanks,

Franco

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
parts:
If you compile only one time a LaTeX file then \ref{} renders in "??". You have to compile twice, without deleting the generated auxiliary file at first compilation (because the compilation reads the file from the beginning to the end, and cannot guess what \ref{} should render if its corresponding \label{} is defined later).

Then you could firstly generate the .tex file using knit() and then compile it twice using texi2pdf().

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
parts:
Note texi2pdf() was designed exactly for this purpose: to compile .tex
with the correct number of times (to resolve all references and
citations). So in theory there is no need to call texi2pdf() twice.

The offending piece might be the extra } in fig.cap="Some text here}",
which will render \caption{Some text here}} in .tex, and that is
invalid LaTeX code.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
parts:
Sorry for the confusion. 

Doing knit2pdf("report.Rnw", texi2dvi="pdflatex") should be equivalent to set the RStudio option "Typeset LaTex into PDF using pdfLaTex".
